notes: Fixture root: evals/fixtures/loop-states — checked in beside this file, one synthetic target per router row, referenced by its repository-relative path. It is not a git repository of its own: the paths sit inside this repository on purpose, because the 2026-07-30 fixture root lived in a session scratchpad and died with it. The records name real commits of this repository (c09675d, 147fa87, b3f98e2), because records-auditor.mjs resolves every sha it reads and refuses one that no pushed ref contains. Eval 3 uses no fixture: it reads the live archived target reviews/archive/015-sameday-shipping, read-only. Fixture invariant: a ledger row is only ever flipped by render-records.mjs, so every fixture whose unit records are deliberately withheld (095, 097) carries its row at its pre-render status with no History line for the round — pre-seeding the flip would both describe a state correct use cannot reach and make the eval's own render write a second History line. Each case carries `setup` and `verify` command lines — extra keys the eval harness ignores and the runner executes: setup restores the fixture to its committed state, verify is what the grader runs to check the tree. Cases 5 and 7 write into the checked-in fixture by design (that is the behaviour under test); their setup restores it first and the runner restores it again afterwards. To rehearse either of them without touching the checked-in fixture, copy the root to evals/.run/ (git-ignored) and point --root there. Tree checks use `git diff --numstat` plus `git ls-files --others`, never a bare `git status`: this repository is checked out with core.autocrlf=true, so a restored fixture file comes back CRLF while the index holds LF and `git status` then reports a modification that no content check can find. On the wrapper's absent test counts and other fixture-specific limits, see each case's expected_output.
